html:
Operation Bootstrap was the plan launched in Puerto Rico in 1947 to industrialise the island by attracting US manufacturers with tax breaks and cheap labour. It was led by the government of Luis Munoz Marin.

Hundreds of factories opened, first making clothes and shoes, later petrochemicals and medicines. Incomes rose fast and Puerto Rico was held up as a showcase of development during the Cold War.

But farm jobs vanished faster than factory jobs came, and hundreds of thousands left for the mainland. When the federal tax breaks ended in 2006, factories closed, which helped bring on the debt crisis.
sum: Operation Bootstrap was the plan launched in Puerto Rico in 1947 to industrialise the island by attracting US manufacturers with tax breaks and cheap labour. It was led by the government of Luis Munoz Marin.
